name: Image Factory Art Foundation (Imagination Factory)
funding: Tiny artist-run non-profit since 1995; former PM Said Musa has given the North Front Street space free for 30 years. No other funders are published.

name: Festival International des Arts du Bénin (FInAB)
funding: Run by Groupe Empire's events arm with Benin government support through its arts fund (FDAC). MTN partnered the 2026 edition, Canal+ Impact 2025. Other partners unnamed; no budget published.

name: Fondation Zinsou
funding: Private, with no Beninese public aid. Its undated patrons page lists BNP Paribas, Masathis, Institut Français de Paris, Agence Française de Développement and Open Society Foundations.

name: Proyecto mARTadero
funding: Its supporters page, dated 2019, names Misereor and Oxfam Internacional as current supporters, and Hivos, Conexión, Solidar Suiza, Cooperación Italiana and CAF as former ones.

name: Espacio Cultural Patiño
funding: Financed by the Patiño foundations: the Bolivian university foundation Simón I. Patiño created in 1931 and the Geneva foundation his heirs set up in 1958.

name: Museo Nacional de Arte de Bolivia
funding: Run since 2003 by the Fundación Cultural del Banco Central de Bolivia, a state foundation.

name: Museo Nacional de Etnografía y Folklore (MUSEF)
funding: State museum (60 years in 2022) funded through the Fundación Cultural del Banco Central de Bolivia, a public body under the central bank.

name: Kiosko Galería
funding: Kiosko is a project of Fundación RSV.

name: Ars Aevi Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: Construction of its planned museum building is funded by the European Union, with contributions from the Government of the Italian Republic, the Canton of Sarajevo and the City of Sarajevo.

name: Botswana National Museum and Art Gallery
funding: Statutory museum set up by Act of Parliament in 1967 and run by the Department of National Museum and Monuments. Government funded its P33 million refurbishment, begun in 2020.

name: Thapong Visual Arts Centre
funding: Board-run centre funded by the Ministry of Youth, Sport and Culture (P2.2M for the 2014 refit). Partners: HB Botswana (2024), BTC Foundation (2018), DTC Botswana and FNB Foundation (2014).

name: Instituto Inhotim
funding: R$ 60M budget. Federal Culture Incentive Law (Lei Rouanet), Vale Cultural Institute civic environmental agreements, and ticket revenues.
